answer: We propose a mechanism where dynamic opportunity-cost bonds enforce capital barriers proportional to the network karst of identity sprawl, rendering the cipher of illicit Sybil multiplication economically irrational. By embedding a subgame-perfect punishment matrix, we ensure that any attempt to harbor multiple personas triggers slashing penalties exceeding staked collateral values, thus forcing a strict Nash equilibrium. Our zero-knowledge verifiable delay utility confirms the negative expected return of collusion, as local adversarial agents converge toward honest participation.
